text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- All civil servants who intend to contest general elections this year must resign by Friday, government says.
- Members of unregistered opposition Islamic Party of Kenya say they will not be drawn into acts of violence during planned June 21 constitutional reform meeting in Mombasa.
- Human Rights Watch/Africa appeals to government to repeal Vagrancy Act to ensure homeless children are not arbitrarily arrested.
- Ethnic Luo leaders endorse opposition parliament member and Luo tribesman Raila Odinga as presidential candidate.
- Family of exiled government critic Sheikh Khalid Balala dispel rumours that Balala is in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania, from where he is to travel by road to Kenya.
- Electoral Commission Chairman Zaccheus Chesoni says his job will not be threatened if he treats all parties equally.
- Thousands hold protest march in Eldoret, one of key towns in President Moi's native Rift Valley, to oppose pro-constitutional reform rally scheduled for Saturday.
